Relative to the card's baseline: family changes from linear (logreg) to gbdt (hist_gbdt), imputation changes from median to none so the model splits on NaN natively, scaling is dropped as irrelevant for trees, class_weight='balanced' is set instead of the baseline's unweighted default, and internal early stopping is disabled so the fit sees all 29,304 training rows.",
  "rationale": "The goal statement is explicit that the remaining distance is on the ranking axis: the bar 0.9194 exceeds 0.8266, the best balanced_accuracy any cut of the baseline's ranking permits, so no threshold-equivalent lever (class_weight alone, on logreg) can reach it — the ranking generator has to change. The cheapest large ranking change available here is a family swap from a linear model to a boosted tree ensemble, which on this kind of mixed numeric<path> table is where the known gains sit: the strong-correlation discrete feature (education-num) and the moderate ones (age, hours-per-week, capital-gain) interact multiplicatively with the low-cardinality categoricals, and capital-gain<path> are highly skewed spike-at-zero columns that a tree can threshold but a standardised linear term cannot. hist_gbdt is the lowest-cost strong tabular learner in the list (cost 3), and 400 iterations at lr 0.06 with 31 leaves is well inside the 600 s / 2048 MB budget on 29k rows. class_weight='balanced' is included because the target is 3.18:1 and the default cut on an unweighted GBDT typically lands at high specificity / low recall, which is exactly what depresses balanced_accuracy; 'balanced' is one known point on that axis, and cut_headroom in the report will say whether a hand-set weight map is worth attempt 2. impute='none' is used because it is available for this family and avoids inventing values in workclass<path> (5.7% worst rate); missing_indicator is deliberately omitted since the card records it as bit-for-bit redundant under impute:none, and missing_count bought nothing measurable. early_stopping=false costs a little overfitting protection but keeps all training rows and makes this attempt's score directly comparable with the baseline and with later attempts; l2_regularization=1.0 and min_samples_leaf=20 guard the extra capacity, and train_val_gap will show if more regularisation is needed next.",
